glossary.def: An Azure AI Search component that pulls from a supported data source on a schedule, detects changes and can run a skillset before writing to an index.
Your code sends documents to the index with the Index Documents API using `upload`, `merge`, `mergeOrUpload` or `delete`.
Reading a database's change log to emit an event for every insert, update and delete.
A messaging guarantee where an event is delivered one or more times, so consumers must tolerate duplicates.
A write that gives the same final state when repeated, usually because the key is derived from the source and the action is an upsert.
A digest of the normalised document or chunk text, used to skip unchanged content and to find duplicates.
A record that marks an item as deleted so downstream stores can remove it, such as a soft-delete flag or a null-valued delete event.
A service-level name that points to an index. Repointing it switches an application to a rebuilt index with no code change.
A side queue for messages that could not be processed, kept for inspection, repair and replay.
A signal or mechanism that slows producers when a downstream stage such as the embedding API cannot keep up.
Detecting reading order, headings, tables, figures and selection marks on a page rather than extracting raw text only.
An Azure service that analyses documents, images, audio and video into schema-defined fields with confidence scores and grounding.
A skillset feature that writes one index document per chunk, linked to its parent by a filterable parent id field.
Building a second index beside the live one, validating it, then switching an alias so rollback stays possible.
Copying a source's permission data onto every chunk at ingest so retrieval can trim results to what the caller may read.

claims.text: The smallest Azure AI Search indexer schedule interval is 5 minutes and the largest is 1,440 minutes.
A push (Index Documents) request carries at most 1,000 documents or 16 MB; HTTP 207 means partial failure, 503 means wait and retry.
`mergeOrUpload` is the usual push action for incremental updates, and `delete` on a missing key is safe so a replayed batch is safe.
Plan for indexer runs that stop at about 2 hours; the limits page lists 2 or 24 hours depending on tier and environment.

GA indexer sources: Blob Storage (ADLS Gen2 through the blob indexer), Cosmos DB for NoSQL, Azure SQL Database, SQL Managed Instance, Table Storage, OneLake. Preview: SharePoint, Azure MySQL, Cosmos DB for MongoDB and Gremlin. Cassandra is unsupported.
Foundry IQ indexed knowledge source kinds generate an indexer pipeline; Azure Blob and OneLake carry no preview label while Azure SQL, File and Indexed SharePoint are preview.
The SharePoint indexer is preview and user-delegated tokens expire every 75 minutes.
Cosmos DB indexer change detection uses a high-water mark on `_ts`; deletion detection needs a top-level Boolean soft-delete field and hard deletes are not seen.
Microsoft Graph and SharePoint Online throttle with 429 or 503 plus a `Retry-After` header; throttled requests count against usage limits.
Blob indexer change detection uses `LastModified`; deletes are not tracked by default and the soft-delete policy must exist from the first run.
A restored soft-deleted blob and a renamed ADLS Gen2 directory are not re-indexed because `LastModified` does not change.
Azure SQL `SqlIntegratedChangeTrackingPolicy` works for tables only, detects deleted rows and is recommended; `HighWaterMarkChangeDetectionPolicy` works for views.
Reset Indexer is GA; Reset Documents, Reset Skills and Resync are preview APIs in `2026-08-01-preview`.
Native blob soft delete works for Blob Storage only (not Azure Files) and requires blob versioning to be off.
Child chunks of a deleted parent in index projections are removed only if the data source has a deletion detection policy.
An index alias is a service-level resource separate from indexes and can be repointed to cut over to a rebuilt index.
You cannot upgrade between Azure OpenAI embedding models in place; new embeddings are required.
The Azure retirement schedule (updated 2026-09-21) lists text-embedding-3-large, 3-small and ada-002 as retiring 2028-02-09; an older page said ada-002 no earlier than April 30, 2026.
The vector index size quota is a memory quota because HNSW graphs are held in memory.
Document Intelligence layout v4.0 `2024-11-30` is GA, returns Markdown with `outputContentFormat=markdown`, renders tables as HTML tables and selection marks as ☒ and ☐.
For Word, Excel, PowerPoint and HTML the layout model extracts embedded text only, not embedded images.
The Document Layout skill defaults to `outputFormat` markdown, times out when a document needs over 5 minutes, and needs a billable Foundry resource beyond 20 documents per indexer per day.
Document Intelligence S0 limits are 500 MB and 2,000 pages per document.
Docling's codebase is MIT licensed, can run locally, and v2.138.0 was released 2026-10-12; Unstructured 0.27.25 was released 2026-10-10.
Content Understanding API `2025-11-01` is GA; `2026-06-01-preview` adds signature detection, document metadata extraction and richer classification.

The Content Understanding skill is GA in search REST `2026-04-01`; semantic chunking is preview (`2026-05-01-preview`); default `maximumLength` is 500 and ranges are 300 to 50,000 characters or 100 to 8,000 tokens.
Content Understanding asynchronous document limit is 200 MB and 300 pages for PDF and images.
Cosmos DB change feed latest version mode omits deletes and keeps only the most recent change per item; all versions and deletes mode needs continuous backup and an opt-in feature flag.
Event Grid delivers at least once with no ordering guarantee; default retry policy is 30 attempts and a 1,440 minute event TTL; dead-lettering applies only if configured.
Debezium delivers at least once and may emit duplicate events after a fault; a delete yields a delete event and, for Kafka compaction, a tombstone.
To fire `BlobCreated` only after a block blob is fully committed, filter on `CopyBlob`, `PutBlob`, `PutBlockList` or `FlushWithClose`.
Service Bus DLQ: default max delivery count is 10, the reason is `MaxDeliveryCountExceeded`, and there is no automatic cleanup.
Azure OpenAI embeddings requests allow at most 2,048 inputs and 300,000 tokens summed across inputs; 429 can occur even when usage metrics appear below quota.
Indexer `maxFailedItems` of -1 continues no matter how many errors occur.
PII Detection skill: `maskingMode` defaults to `none` and `replace` returns `maskedText`; `minimumPrecision` defaults to 0.0; `maskingCharacter` defaults to `*`; `domain` is `phi` or `none`.

Knowledge source `ingestionPermissionOptions` (for example `userIds`, `groupIds`) requires `2026-08-01-preview` and is not supported on `2026-04-01`; projections must copy ACL fields onto every chunk.
ADLS Gen2 POSIX-like ACL and RBAC scope ingestion is preview.
